messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Offer from Redwood Inference

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time to meet with the infra team last week. We enjoyed the conversation and are excited about the possibility of you joining Redwood Inference as Senior Infrastructure Engineer.

Attached is the formal offer (GR-Offer-v2.pdf) reflecting the total compensation discussed: base 170,000 GBP, target OTE 220,000 GBP with a 12% RSU grant vesting over 4 years, and standard benefits. This offer assumes EU/UK location (geo band: LDN-EU).

We'd love to get your decision within the next 7 days to keep the proposed start date in late May, but we're happy to be flexible within reason — let me know if you have questions or need context for any line items.

Attachments: GR-Offer-v2.pdf (Offer Letter, 42KB)

Best,
Grace O'Connor

From: Alex Chen <alex@streamline.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@talentpartner.co>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:48:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Offer from Redwood Inference

Hi Grace —

Appreciate the offer and the quick turnaround. Two quick points: first, I have a competing in-house offer from a London-based startup that has given me a signing deadline of 48 hours (they put forward a slightly higher base to offset the RSU mix). Second, the competing offer lists a geo premium for London which puts cash on par with what I need for relocation/logistics.

I love Redwood's mission and the team — the role is my top choice — but I need to be able to present a final number to the other team within two days. Would Redwood be open to revisiting the LDN geo band to bridge ~12k GBP in base so I can accept here instead? If legal/comp can’t move base, I’d consider a one-time sign-on to make the economics align.

If easier, we can take a quick call this evening (UK time) — Maya (cc'd) is my recruiter and can help coordinate.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chen
Principal Engineer (candidate)
alex@streamline.ai

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Candidate request — Alex Chen (competing offer, 48h)

Marissa / Karthik —

Looping you both on an urgent candidate situation. Alex (candidate) just shared he has a competing offer with a 48-hour decision window and asked for a ~12k GBP uplift to the base or a one-time sign-on to match the economics. He is strongly preferring Redwood.

Notes:
- Role: Senior Infrastructure Engineer, team: Serving Runtime (hired by Karthik).
- Current offer: base 170k GBP, OTE 220k GBP, 12% RSU.
- Request: +12k GBP base OR one-time sign-on (amount flexible), and decision within 48h.
- Candidate is UK-based (would be LDN-EU geo band).

I’ve attached the offer and a quick comparables sheet (Candidate-Comparables.xlsx) showing local market comps and the comp-band-approval.pdf that outlines allowable uplift thresholds.

Attachments: GR-Offer-v2.pdf; Candidate-Comparables.xlsx; Comp-band-approval.pdf

Can we get a quick decision on whether we can: 1) approve a 12k base uplift; 2) alternatively approve a sign-on payment (pro-rated) to close; or 3) agree to an accelerated sign window but keep the current numbers? Karthik — what's your preference given the candidate fit?

Thanks,
Grace

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Candidate request — Alex Chen (competing offer, 48h)

Grace / Marissa —

Thanks for flagging. Short answer: I want Alex on the team. He checked all the technical boxes and would materially accelerate our infra roadmap. That said, we need to be thoughtful about precedent and banding.

Proposal: Approve a one-time sign-on of 12,000 GBP paid in two installments (50% at start, 50% after 6 months) rather than moving the base. This keeps comp band intact and avoids inflation of base for future hires. It meets the candidate's ask on net cash while preserving internal comp guardrails.

Constraints: We can only approve sign-ons up to 15k at manager level if budget exists; anything higher needs comp committee. Jonas — can you confirm headcount and budget availability from the 2Q reserved pool? If yes, I authorize the sign-on and will take ownership of communicating performance expectations during onboarding.

I recommend we give the candidate an updated offer with sign-on and a 48-hour signing window to beat the external deadline.

-Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 18:03:00 +0100
Subject: Revised offer and sign-on — Redwood Inference (48h window)

Alex —

Thank you for your patience while we coordinated internally. We’re excited to make this work. Per Karthik's approval, Redwood can offer a one-time sign-on of 12,000 GBP (paid 50% at start, 50% at six months). We will not be increasing base pay in this instance so the base remains 170,000 GBP; the sign-on is intended to match the near-term cash profile you described.

I’ve attached an updated offer (GR-Offer-v2_signedon.pdf) that includes the sign-on language and the DocuSign link below. We’d appreciate a signed acceptance within 48 hours to honor the timeline you shared; if you need to talk through details, Karthik and I are available for a short call this evening (we can do 7pm BST).

DocuSign: https://docusign.example/GR-2027-042
Attachments: GR-Offer-v2.pdf (updated with sign-on clause); Comp-band-approval.pdf

Please let me know if you want the sign-on paid as a lump sum instead of installments and I can check with payroll, but manager authorization is currently for the two-installment structure.

Looking forward to welcoming you aboard — hope we can close this today.

Best,
